messages.body_plain:
ANWB Ledenaanbieding

De hitte is terug.
Maar jij staat klaar.



Hoi [first_name|daar],

De voorspellingen liegen er niet om: nog weken warm weer. Wat dat betekent  
voor jou onderweg? Lauwe drankjes, gesmolten chocola en een auto die  
aanvoelt als een sauna.

Tenzij je slimmer bent dan het weer.



ANWB Elektrische Autokoelbox


Koelt tot 18?C onder omgevingstemperatuur
Stil en energiezuinig via het 12V-stopcontact
Inhoud 15 liter ? ruimte voor 20 blikjes
Lichtgewicht, compacte tas met draagriem
Getest en goedgekeurd door de ANWB



Of je nu naar het strand rijdt, de kinderen ophaalt na sport of een  
weekendje weg plant ? deze koelbox past op de achterbank, in de kofferbak,  
of gewoon naast je stoel.


Bekijk de aanbieding ?


Op = op. Beschikbaar zolang de voorraad strekt.



Dit is een commerci?le mededeling. Je ontvangt dit bericht omdat je op onze  
mailinglijst staat. Wil je geen e-mails meer ontvangen? Uitschrijven.

messages.body_plain:
Source: r-cran-rnetcdf
Version: 2.11-1-2
Severity: serious
Control: close -1 2.11-2-1
Tags: sid forky
User: release.debian.org at packages.debian.org
Usertags: out-of-sync

Dear maintainer(s),

The Release Team considers packages that are out-of-sync between testing and unstable for more than 30 days as having a Release Critical bug in testing [1]. Your package src:r-cran-rnetcdf has been trying to migrate for 32 days [2], hence this bug report. The current output of the migration software for this package is copied to the bottom of this report and should list the reason why the package is blocked. Regularly, reporting issues against reverse (build/test/regular) dependencies is what needs to happen. If this has already been done, than this bug is just for tracking purposes.

If a package is out of sync between unstable and testing for a longer period, this usually means that bugs in the package in testing cannot be fixed via unstable. Blocked packages can have impact on other packages, which makes preparing for the release more difficult. The situation that caused this bug report might even be the result of such an issue. We expect maintainers to fix issues that hamper the migration of their package in a timely manner. If your package in this situation due to another package, consider helping out.

This bug will trigger auto-removal when appropriate. As with all new bugs, there will be at least 30 days before the package is auto-removed.

This bug submission immediately closes the bug with the version in unstable, so if that version or a later version migrates, this bug will no longer affect testing. This bug is also tagged to only affect sid and forky, so it doesn't affect (old-)stable.

If you believe your package is unable to migrate to testing due to issues beyond your control, don't hesitate to contact the Release Team.

This bug report has been automatically generated. If you have any comments with regards to the content or the process, please reach out to me.

Paul

[1] https://lists.debian.org/debian-devel-announce/2023/06/msg00001.html

messages.subject: [R-pkg-team] Bug#1150390: r-bioc-ballgown: autopkgtest fails with testthat 3.3.2: could not find function "is_true"
messages.subject_clean: [R-pkg-team] Bug#1150390: r-bioc-ballgown: autopkgtest fails with testthat 3.3.2: could not find function "is_true"
messages.body_plain:
Source: r-bioc-ballgown
Version: 2.43.0+dfsg-2
Severity: normal
Tags: patch
X-Debbugs-Cc: seb128 at ubuntu.com
User: ubuntu-devel at lists.ubuntu.com
Usertags: origin-ubuntu  ubuntu-patch

Hi,

The package builds fine, but its autopkgtest fails with testthat 3.3.2,
which removed the long-deprecated is_true() expectation. This blocks
migration to testing:

  > test_check('ballgown')
  Saving _problems/test-annotation-42.R
  [ FAIL 1 | WARN 32 | SKIP 0 | PASS 127 ]

  ?? Failed tests ??
  ?? Error ('test-annotation.R:41:5'): splitting attribute fields works ??
  Error in `is_true()`: could not find function "is_true"
  Backtrace:
      ?
   1. ??testthat::expect_that(...) at test-annotation.R:41:5

Ubuntu sees the same failure.

Upstream fixed this by replacing both is_true() calls in
tests/testthat/test-annotation.R with equals(TRUE):

  https://github.com/alyssafrazee/ballgown/commit/0ccd85f97c942de7e93a3f9b341fe688a6b4bb88

The attached patch is that commit as a quilt patch, unchanged. It only
touches the test file. We are applying it in Ubuntu as
2.43.0+dfsg-2ubuntu1.

Cheers,
Sebastien


-- System Information:
Debian Release: forky/sid
  APT prefers resolute-updates
  APT policy: (500, 'resolute-updates'), (500, 'resolute-security'), (500, 'resolute'), (100, 'resolute-backports')
Architecture: amd64 (x86_64)

Kernel: Linux 7.0.0-38-generic (SMP w/16 CPU threads; PREEMPT)
Kernel taint flags: TAINT_PROPRIETARY_MODULE, TAINT_WARN, TAINT_OOT_MODULE
Locale: LANG=fr_FR.UTF-8, LC_CTYPE=fr_FR.UTF-8 (charmap=UTF-8), LANGUAGE not set
Shell: /bin/sh linked to /usr/bin/dash
Init: systemd (via /run/systemd/system)
LSM: AppArmor: enabled
-------------- next part --------------
Description: Replace is_true() removed from testthat
 testthat 3.3.2 removed the long-deprecated is_true() expectation, so
 test-annotation.R fails with 'could not find function "is_true"'.
 Use equals(TRUE) instead.
Origin: upstream, https://github.com/alyssafrazee/ballgown/commit/0ccd85f97c942de7e93a3f9b341fe688a6b4bb88
Last-Update: 2026-10-09
---
Index: r-bioc-ballgown-2.43.0+dfsg/tests/testthat/test-annotation.R
===================================================================
--- r-bioc-ballgown-2.43.0+dfsg.orig/tests/testthat/test-annotation.R
+++ r-bioc-ballgown-2.43.0+dfsg/tests/testthat/test-annotation.R
@@ -39,14 +39,14 @@ test_that('splitting attribute fields wo
     expect_that(getAttributeField(x$attributes, 'transcript_id'), 
         not(throws_error()))
     expect_that(all(is.na(getAttributeField(x$seqname, 'transcript_id'))), 
-        is_true())
+        equals(TRUE))
     transcripts = getAttributeField(x$attributes, 'transcript_id')
     expect_that(transcripts, is_a('character'))
     expect_that(length(transcripts), equals(13732))
     expect_that(transcripts[192], equals('ENST00000444520'))
     expect_that(all(is.na(getAttributeField(x$attributes, 'transcript_id', 
         attrsep=','))), 
-        is_true())
+        equals(TRUE))
 })

messages.subject: [R-pkg-team] Bug#1150839: src:r-cran-xts: fails to migrate to testing for too long
messages.subject_clean: [R-pkg-team] Bug#1150839: src:r-cran-xts: fails to migrate to testing for too long
messages.body_plain:
Source: r-cran-xts
Version: 0.14.2-4
Severity: serious
Control: close -1 0.14.3-1
Tags: sid forky
User: release.debian.org at packages.debian.org
Usertags: out-of-sync

Dear maintainer(s),

The Release Team considers packages that are out-of-sync between testing and unstable for more than 30 days as having a Release Critical bug in testing [1]. Your package src:r-cran-xts has been trying to migrate for 32 days [2], hence this bug report. The current output of the migration software for this package is copied to the bottom of this report and should list the reason why the package is blocked. Regularly, reporting issues against reverse (build/test/regular) dependencies is what needs to happen. If this has already been done, than this bug is just for tracking purposes.

If a package is out of sync between unstable and testing for a longer period, this usually means that bugs in the package in testing cannot be fixed via unstable. Blocked packages can have impact on other packages, which makes preparing for the release more difficult. The situation that caused this bug report might even be the result of such an issue. We expect maintainers to fix issues that hamper the migration of their package in a timely manner. If your package in this situation due to another package, consider helping out.

This bug will trigger auto-removal when appropriate. As with all new bugs, there will be at least 30 days before the package is auto-removed.

This bug submission immediately closes the bug with the version in unstable, so if that version or a later version migrates, this bug will no longer affect testing. This bug is also tagged to only affect sid and forky, so it doesn't affect (old-)stable.

If you believe your package is unable to migrate to testing due to issues beyond your control, don't hesitate to contact the Release Team.

This bug report has been automatically generated. If you have any comments with regards to the content or the process, please reach out to me.

Paul

[1] https://lists.debian.org/debian-devel-announce/2023/06/msg00001.html
[2] https://qa.debian.org/excuses.php?package=r-cran-xts

messages.subject_clean: [R-pkg-team] Bug#1152396: src:r-cran-guerry: fails to migrate to testing for too long
messages.body_plain:
Source: r-cran-guerry
Version: 1.8.3-2
Severity: serious
Control: close -1 1.8.5-1
Tags: sid forky
User: release.debian.org at packages.debian.org
Usertags: out-of-sync

Dear maintainer(s),

The Release Team considers packages that are out-of-sync between testing and unstable for more than 30 days as having a Release Critical bug in testing [1]. Your package src:r-cran-guerry has been trying to migrate for 31 days [2], hence this bug report. The current output of the migration software for this package is copied to the bottom of this report and should list the reason why the package is blocked. Regularly, reporting issues against reverse (build/test/regular) dependencies is what needs to happen. If this has already been done, than this bug is just for tracking purposes.

If a package is out of sync between unstable and testing for a longer period, this usually means that bugs in the package in testing cannot be fixed via unstable. Blocked packages can have impact on other packages, which makes preparing for the release more difficult. The situation that caused this bug report might even be the result of such an issue. We expect maintainers to fix issues that hamper the migration of their package in a timely manner. If your package in this situation due to another package, consider helping out.

This bug will trigger auto-removal when appropriate. As with all new bugs, there will be at least 30 days before the package is auto-removed.

This bug submission immediately closes the bug with the version in unstable, so if that version or a later version migrates, this bug will no longer affect testing. This bug is also tagged to only affect sid and forky, so it doesn't affect (old-)stable.

If you believe your package is unable to migrate to testing due to issues beyond your control, don't hesitate to contact the Release Team.

This bug report has been automatically generated. If you have any comments with regards to the content or the process, please reach out to me.

Paul

[1] https://lists.debian.org/debian-devel-announce/2023/06/msg00001.html
[2] https://qa.debian.org/excuses.php?package=r-cran-guerry

Current text from [2]:
Migration status for r-cran-guerry (1.8.3-2 to 1.8.5-1): BLOCKED: Rejected/violates migration policy/introduces a regression
Issues preventing migration:
? ? Reproducibility regression on amd64: r-cran-guerry
? ? Reproducibility regression on arm64: r-cran-guerry
? ? Reproducibility regression on armhf: r-cran-guerry
? ? Reproducibility regression on i386: r-cran-guerry
? ? Not built on buildd: arch all binaries uploaded by plessy, a new source-only upload is needed to allow migration
Additional info (not blocking):
? ? Piuparts tested OK - https://piuparts.debian.org/sid/source/r/r-cran-guerry.html

? ? Autopkgtest skipped on i386: not installable (which is allowed)
? ? Autopkgtest skipped on s390x: not installable (which is allowed)
